chunks: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The bequest is truth, and the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) had made a bequest, so it is befitting for the Muslim that he bequeaths.'

key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةُ: The bequest/will (wasiyya) — a legal declaration of one's wishes for property or affairs after death
key_terms.حَقٌّ: Truth, right, or established obligation — affirming the legitimacy and validity of the bequest
key_terms.يَنْبَغِي: It is befitting, appropriate, or recommended — indicating a strong normative recommendation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about making a bequest (wasiyya) in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) affirms the legitimacy and recommendability of making a bequest (wasiyya) in Islam, grounding it in prophetic precedent. The hadith establishes both the truth-value (haqq) of the bequest as a religious institution and the normative expectation that Muslims should follow the Prophet's example by making their own bequests. The audience — early Shi'i scholars studying inheritance law — would have understood this as a foundational statement for the chapter on wills and bequests.
